question: In 1970s Vermont, what best predicted whether a child would have their tonsils taken out?
answer: Which surgeons practised nearby. Wennberg and Gittelsohn mapped Vermont's hospital areas and found tonsil removal rates differing several-fold between neighbouring towns with similar populations. The local supply and habits of doctors tracked the operations far better than any measure of illness. A child's tonsils depended more on the town than on the throat.
move: When rates vary wildly between similar places, look at who decides, not who receives.
ask: Is the advice I get shaped more by the person giving it than by my own situation?
reference: Wennberg & Gittelsohn, Small area variations in health care delivery, Science, 1973
